narrative.summaryIntro:
Somnath Temple, located at Prabhas in Gujarat, is the first among the twelve Jyotirlingas—the holiest shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva. Positioned at the confluence of the Veraval River and the Arabian Sea, the temple holds immense spiritual significance in Hinduism. According to legend, Chandra (the Moon God) worshipped Shiva here, earning the site its sacred status.

The temple has been destroyed and rebuilt multiple times throughout history. The current structure was rebuilt in 1951 after independence, featuring exquisite stone carvings and Chalukya architectural style. It stands as a symbol of Hindu resilience and spiritual devotion, attracting millions of pilgrims and tourists annually.
